agent_note: First-person present-tense narration (legal/innocence-project register) with an identifiable past strand: case backstory and forensic-expert history (q03503, q03504, q03506, q03509, q03510, q03516). Event 15 (9 present / 6 past = 60% present), gnomic 10, dialogue 0, paratext 0, unclear 0. beat_tense: ZERO quotes bucketed dialogue, so the field is unexercised in this book -- no quote in the sample is majority-speech. Mark signal: quotation marks DO survive this extraction (q03518 carries intact curly quotes around 'Are you sure?'), so mark-absence elsewhere is more informative than the methodology's default assumption; I nonetheless cross-checked the unmarked candidates (q03500, q03507, q03512) on vocative/direct-address/register and found no speech markers. The clearest tense evidence the old beat rule would have discarded is the present tag 'he asks' in q03518, which survives here only because that quote is majority-narration and therefore bucketed event rather than dialogue. Split is 60/40 with a structural cause (case-history strand), so this is a Mixed--strand finding, not high-confidence present.
